text:
lucy: Build alert: prod linkcheck found several 404 fragments after the mkdocs->mdx migration. Example: /getting-started/auth#token-rotation is reported missing even though the heading is present.

anand: We should check for three common causes: invisible unicode (soft hyphen/ZW), duplicated IDs from frontmatter + heading, and our legacy redirect list not updated.

mike: Quick triage steps I ran:
1) hex-dump the heading line to reveal invisible chars:
   `xxd -g 1 -l 80 docs/getting-started/auth.md | sed -n '1,3p'`
2) run our two sluggers and diff outputs:
   `node ./scripts/slug-compare.js "Token rotation"`
I found a U+00AD after "token-" and the legacy slug collapsed the hyphen, producing a different anchor.

lucy: Good find. Also noticed a stray frontmatter title on some migrated pages; when the page title and the first H2 both produce ids, Docusaurus sometimes appends `-1` to the generated id which breaks old links.

anand: Plan: 
- Add a small normalize-headings.sh to strip U+00AD/U+200B/U+200C/U+FEFF before slug generation.
- Update the migration tool to remove duplicate frontmatter titles when a canonical H1/H2 exists.
- Generate redirect mappings for anchors that differ, but only for anchors that appear in the inbound-links export to avoid bloating redirect tables.
- Add a docs-ci job `slug-compare` that runs on docs changes and fails if any heading produces mismatched slugs between our legacy slugify and Docusaurus's slugger.

mike: I'll open a PR with the normalization script + redirect generator and a small unit test that injects invisible chars and emoji into headings to assert parity.

docs-bot: New PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5799 by mike  heading normalization + redirect generator + slug-compare CI

linkcheck-bot: Docs CI: linkcheck flagged 4 missing fragments. Rerun after PR merges.

lucy: Thanks all. If you find other pages with weird anchors (especially migrated from mkdocs), paste them here and we'll add them to the redirect whitelist. :thumbsup:
